attractions.name: Panama Canal
attractions.desc: One of the most significant engineering achievements of the 20th century, this canal cuts across the isthmus to connect the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, saving ships weeks of travel around South America. The Miraflores Locks visitor center allows visitors to watch massive container ships rise and fall through the lock system up close. Its ongoing expansion has kept it central to global shipping well into the present day.

attractions.name: Casco Viejo, Panama City
attractions.desc: Panama City's restored colonial old quarter, its Spanish and French colonial buildings now housing boutique hotels, rooftop bars, and restaurants alongside older churches and plazas. The contrast with the modern skyscraper skyline visible just across the bay is one of the city's most striking views. It's a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the natural base for exploring the capital.

attractions.name: San Blas Islands
attractions.desc: An archipelago of over 350 small islands in the Guna Yala comarca, governed autonomously by the indigenous Guna people who maintain strict control over tourism development. Many islands are little more than a strip of white sand and a few palm trees, offering an unspoiled contrast to more developed Caribbean destinations. Visits typically require staying in simple, community-run accommodations rather than resorts.

attractions.name: Boquete
attractions.desc: A cool mountain town in Panama's highlands, known for coffee farms producing some of the world's most expensive beans, geisha varietals grown at high altitude. Hiking trails here include the Quetzal Trail, named for the elusive, brightly colored bird sometimes spotted in the cloud forest. Its cooler climate offers a welcome break from the tropical heat of the coasts.

attractions.name: Bocas del Toro
attractions.desc: A Caribbean archipelago known for surf breaks, mangrove channels, and a laid-back, slightly bohemian island culture distinct from the rest of the country. Water taxis connect the main town to quieter islands with beaches and snorkeling spots. It's a common stop for travelers continuing overland toward Costa Rica.

attractions.name: Embera indigenous villages
attractions.desc: River communities in Panama's rainforest interior that welcome visitors for cultural visits involving traditional dance, craft demonstrations, and a dugout canoe journey to reach the village itself. It offers a direct, community-led way to learn about one of Panama's indigenous groups. Visits are usually arranged as a guided day trip from Panama City.

itinerary.label: Days 1–3
itinerary.title: Panama City
itinerary.desc: The Panama Canal locks, Casco Viejo's old town, and an Embera village visit.
itinerary.cost: The Miraflores Locks visitor center costs about $20; an Embera village visit typically runs $60–90 including transport and lunch.
itinerary.food: Try a sancocho, Panama's national stew, at a traditional fonda in Casco Viejo.

itinerary.label: Days 4–5
itinerary.title: Boquete
itinerary.desc: Coffee farm tours and hiking in the cool highland cloud forest.
itinerary.cost: A coffee farm tour, including tastings, costs about $30–40, more for geisha-specific tours.
itinerary.food: Try Panamanian coffee at its source — a proper geisha cup can be a genuine splurge worth having once.

itinerary.label: Days 6–9
itinerary.title: Bocas del Toro or San Blas
itinerary.desc: Either Caribbean island time in Bocas or a more remote trip to the San Blas Islands.
itinerary.logistics: ~30min flight from Boquete to Bocas del Toro
itinerary.cost: A multi-day San Blas island-hopping boat trip runs $100–180/day including basic accommodation and meals; Bocas day tours cost $25–40.
itinerary.food: In San Blas, meals are typically included and prepared by local Guna families — fresh fish and coconut rice are common.

goodToKnow.safety: Very safe in Panama City and main tourist areas
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Domestic flights connect Bocas del Toro and remote regions quickly
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Tocumen International Airport (PTY) in Panama City is the country's main gateway

food.name: Sancocho
food.desc: A hearty chicken and root vegetable stew, considered Panama's national dish.

food.name: Ceviche
food.desc: Fresh fish cured in lime juice, sold at stalls throughout Panama City's fish market.

food.name: Patacones
food.desc: Twice-fried green plantains, a common side dish across the country.

food.name: Panamanian coffee
food.desc: Includes some of the world's most sought-after and expensive geisha varietals, grown in Boquete.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Panama?
faq.a: Not for most Western passport holders (EU, UK, US, Canada) for short stays, typically up to 90–180 days depending on nationality.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Tocumen International (PTY) in Panama City, the country's main gateway.

faq.q: Can I really watch ships transit the Panama Canal?
faq.a: Yes — the Miraflores Locks visitor center has viewing decks timed around actual ship transits, worth checking the schedule before you go.

faq.q: Bocas del Toro or San Blas — which should I choose?
faq.a: Bocas is easier to reach and has more infrastructure and nightlife. San Blas is more remote, run by the indigenous Guna people, and offers a quieter, more traditional island experience.

daysReason: 9 days covers Panama City, Boquete, and a choice between Bocas del Toro or San Blas without rushing. 5–6 works for just Panama City and one region; 11+ lets you do both island regions instead of choosing.
visa: Not required for EU, UK, US, and Canadian citizens for short stays — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Canal do Panamá
attractions.desc: Uma das conquistas de engenharia mais significativas do século XX, este canal atravessa o istmo para ligar os Oceanos Atlântico e Pacífico, poupando aos navios semanas de viagem à volta da América do Sul. O centro de visitantes das Eclusas de Miraflores permite aos visitantes observar de perto navios porta-contentores maciços a subir e descer pelo sistema de eclusas. A sua expansão contínua tem-no mantido central para o transporte marítimo global até ao presente.

attractions.name: Casco Viejo, Cidade do Panamá
attractions.desc: O bairro colonial antigo restaurado da Cidade do Panamá, com os seus edifícios coloniais espanhóis e franceses a albergar hoje hotéis boutique, bares na cobertura, e restaurantes ao lado de igrejas e praças mais antigas. O contraste com o horizonte moderno de arranha-céus visível mesmo do outro lado da baía é uma das vistas mais marcantes da cidade. É Património Mundial da UNESCO e a base natural para explorar a capital.

attractions.name: Ilhas San Blas
attractions.desc: Um arquipélago de mais de 350 pequenas ilhas na comarca de Guna Yala, governada de forma autónoma pelo povo indígena Guna, que mantém controlo rígido sobre o desenvolvimento turístico. Muitas ilhas não são mais do que uma faixa de areia branca e algumas palmeiras, oferecendo um contraste intocado face a destinos caribenhos mais desenvolvidos. As visitas tipicamente requerem alojamento simples gerido pela comunidade em vez de resorts.

attractions.name: Boquete
attractions.desc: Uma fresca cidade de montanha nas terras altas do Panamá, conhecida por quintas de café produzindo alguns dos grãos mais caros do mundo, variedades geisha cultivadas em alta altitude. Trilhos de caminhada aqui incluem o Trilho do Quetzal, batizado pela ave esquiva e vivamente colorida por vezes avistada na floresta de nuvens. O seu clima mais fresco oferece uma pausa bem-vinda do calor tropical das costas.

attractions.name: Bocas del Toro
attractions.desc: Um arquipélago caribenho conhecido pelas ondas de surf, canais de mangal, e uma cultura de ilha descontraída e ligeiramente boémia distinta do resto do país. Táxis aquáticos ligam a cidade principal a ilhas mais tranquilas com praias e locais de snorkel. É uma paragem comum para viajantes a continuar por terra em direção à Costa Rica.

attractions.name: Aldeias indígenas Emberá
attractions.desc: Comunidades ribeirinhas no interior de floresta tropical do Panamá que recebem visitantes para visitas culturais envolvendo dança tradicional, demonstrações de artesanato, e uma viagem de canoa escavada até à própria aldeia. Oferece uma forma direta e liderada pela comunidade de aprender sobre um dos grupos indígenas do Panamá. As visitas são normalmente organizadas como excursão guiada de um dia a partir da Cidade do Panamá.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–3
itinerary.title: Cidade do Panamá
itinerary.desc: As eclusas do Canal do Panamá, a cidade antiga de Casco Viejo, e uma visita a uma aldeia Emberá.

itinerary.label: Dias 4–5
itinerary.title: Boquete
itinerary.desc: Excursões a quintas de café e caminhadas na floresta de nuvens das terras altas frescas.
itinerary.logistics: ~45min de voo desde a Cidade do Panamá

itinerary.label: Dias 6–9
itinerary.title: Bocas del Toro ou San Blas
itinerary.desc: Ou tempo de ilha caribenho em Bocas, ou uma viagem mais remota às Ilhas San Blas.
itinerary.logistics: ~30min de voo desde Boquete até Bocas del Toro

goodToKnow.safety: Muito seguro na Cidade do Panamá e nas principais zonas turísticas
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Voos domésticos ligam rapidamente Bocas del Toro e regiões remotas
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Tocumen International Airport (PTY) in Panama City is the country's main gateway

food.name: Sancocho
food.desc: Um guisado substancial de frango e raízes, considerado o prato nacional do Panamá.

food.name: Ceviche
food.desc: Peixe fresco curado em sumo de lima, vendido em bancas no mercado de peixe da Cidade do Panamá.

food.name: Patacones
food.desc: Bananas verdes fritas duas vezes, um acompanhamento comum em todo o país.

food.name: Café panamiano
food.desc: Inclui algumas das variedades geisha mais procuradas e caras do mundo, cultivadas em Boquete.
